test_title: SSC Selection Post 2024 (Graduate Level) Official Paper (Held On: 20 Jun, 2024 Shift 3)
subject: general
question: Which Article of the Indian Constitution mentions that ‘In the performance of his/her duties, the Attorney-General for India shall have the right of audience in all the courts in the territory of India’?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Article 76(3)**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Article 76(3)** of the Indian Constitution states that "In the performance of his/her duties, the Attorney-General for India shall have the right of audience in all the courts in the territory of India."
 
• The Attorney-General for India is the chief legal advisor to the Government of India and is appointed by the President of India under Article 76.
 
• The Attorney-General has the right to speak and take part in the proceedings of both Houses of Parliament but does not have the right to vote.
 
• This provision ensures that the Attorney-General can effectively represent the government in legal matters across all courts in India.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The **Attorney-General for India** is the highest law officer in the country and must be a person qualified to be appointed as a Judge of the Supreme Court.
 
• The Attorney-General's duties include giving advice to the Government of India upon legal matters, and performing other legal duties as assigned by the President.
 
• The Attorney-General represents the Government of India in all cases in the Supreme Court in which the Government of India is concerned.
 
• The position of the Attorney-General is not a full-time position, and the officeholder can practice privately as well, provided the other legal work does not conflict with the duties as Attorney-General.
